_comment: Interpretive overlay for the Swiss-cheese defence-in-depth view (Phase 2).
EMPTY BY DEFAULT AND HIDDEN IN THE UI. Nothing here comes from the verified matrix.
A Swiss-cheese model needs three things: an ordered set of defensive layers, layers
that are roughly independent of each other, and holes in each layer against a specific
hazard. Only the third is in data/atlas.json, a weak tier is a big hole. The ordering
and the independence assumption are editorial research judgments that the workbook does
not contain, and the dataset's own reading note argues these defences are correlated:
the load-bearing problems all lean on measurement and oversight, and the single Robust
cell (sandboxing against P7) inherits its reliability from ordinary systems security.
So: authoring layers here is a research claim, not a configuration step. Add layers only
once you can defend the ordering and say something honest about the correlation between
them. Hole sizes stay derived from the matrix; the caveat below stays on screen.
To author: set enabled to true and add layers, outermost defence first. Each member is
an area tag (EA, IN, AR, DS, SO, AF, CE, SA, SH, ST, SM, TG) or an agenda id (EA1, DS3, ...).
"rationale": "why this sits here in the order", "members": ["DS", "SH2"] }
caveat: Layer ordering and independence are editorial assumptions, not results from the verified matrix; the underlying data suggests these defences are correlated.
